# TypeScript cases that are red under genuinely split product and instance
# roots, and green in a fused checkout.  One test name per line, then the
# issue that owns the answer.
#
# These are NOT known-bad tests.  They are the same open precedence question
# the Python ledger records: each fixture builds its own instance layer, writes
# `allowedAdapters: []` into it and passes `AGENTS_HOME` explicitly, but then
# spreads `...process.env` without clearing `AGENT_FABRIC_INSTANCE_ROOT`.  Under
# split roots that ambient variable outranks the explicit `AGENTS_HOME`, so the
# CLI reads the job's provisioned instance instead of the fixture's, finds real
# adapters in `allowedAdapters`, and reaches for a provider executable the
# fixture never allowed.
#
# The tests encode one answer to which of the two wins and the runtime
# implements the other.  #563 owns choosing; this rig must not settle it by
# annotation.  When #563 lands, the inverse gate below turns these green, the
# assertion on the failure count breaks, and the entries must be deleted in
# that same pull request.
bootstraps, starts from daemon idle, adds one narrow peer, and replays as a no-op #563
converges concurrent optional seat additions without silently dropping either seat #563
recovers an expired provisioned roster with the advertised renewal command #563
keeps chair-seat and revoked-lease failures on their real enforcement paths #563
rejects a live non-bootstrap capability on the expired-roster rebind gate #563
starts the on-demand daemon when provisioning begins from the healthy idle state #563
